ops.title: Trust.Business widens to []Requirement — an app plus its extension is an ordinary shape
ops.body:
Decided by yasyf, 2026-08-01, after the Swift/fusekit collapse investigation.

`Trust.Business` was a single `*Requirement` carrying exactly one `SigningIdentifier`.
`Requirement.Validate()` correctly refuses a TeamID-only requirement ("same-team lateral
authority"), but "exactly one identity" is an under-generalization, not a deliberate narrowing: an
app plus its extension is an ordinary macOS shape, and fusekit's business lane must admit two
genuinely different signed bundles — the broker/status app (`com.yasyf.cc-pool.status`) and its File
Provider extension (`com.yasyf.cc-pool.status.fileprovider`).

**`Trust.Business` becomes `[]Requirement`** — admitted if ANY element matches. An OR over
explicitly enumerated full requirements stays strictly stronger than the TeamID-only case Validate()
already refuses; each disjunct still carries its own entitlements and app group, which matters here
because a File Provider extension's entitlements differ from its host's.

The two escapes were rejected. Collapsing the FPE's pin onto the host's identity is a change to
cc-pool's *signed artifact* rather than its source, and it makes the host and the extension mutually
substitutable to the daemon — a trust regression, not a refactor. Moving `broker.open` off the daemon
socket is architecturally tidiest but is the largest possible fusekit change during a migration that
already rewrites its whole daemonkit surface.

Implementation notes:
- Design v2 §3.3 freezes `Trust`; this amends it. Lane D (business lane) owns it.
- `Requirement.Digest()` must stay stable across a set: canonicalize the order (the existing
  precedent is sorting entitlement keys before hashing) so an unordered set does not produce two
  digests. Consumers bake these digests — cc-notes' `RequireDaemonkitStopReceipt`, captain-hook's
  `RequireExactStopReceipt`, and cc-notes' golden hash at deployment_identity_test.go:136.
- `Trust.Control` stays a single `*Requirement`: the control lane admits exactly one session
  server-wide (`internal/wire/server.go:105` `controlSlot`), so a set there would model nothing.
